links.outcome: ESI discordance and clinically significant errors after fine-tuning on institutional pediatric triage data vs baseline models
links.effect: Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B substantially reduced discordance and clinically significant errors, outperforming all baseline SLMs and GPT-4o (no numbers in abstract).
links.quote: Through large-scale domain adaptation using expert-curated and silver-standard pediatric triage data, fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B models substantially reduced discordance and clinically significant errors, outperforming all baseline SLMs and advanced proprietary large language models (LLMs, e.g., GPT-4o).

unlisted_practices: Using clinical vignette summaries of triage narratives as the prompting pipeline for ESI prediction
Using open-source small language models for privacy-preserving on-premise triage decision support

screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates domain-adapted small language models (SLMs) against standard proprietary models for emergency department triage (ESI assignment) on clinical narratives. It focuses on model development, prompting pipelines, and fine-tuning rather than testing an organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
